newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks firm amid continued uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks firm amid continued uncertainty.

text.p: Colombian stocks rose Thursday amid continued uncertainty about the looming U.S. decision on whether to certify Colombia as a trustworthy ally in the drug war or blacklist it for a second year.
Bogota's IBB index rose 0.21 percent to 1064.57 amid a 1 billion peso volume, while Medellin's IBOMED general price index closed at 16,787.56, up 0.51 percent amid a 2 billion peso trade.
"Trading was relatively thin and there were a lot of cross deals in little-traded shares as investors took advantage of the uncertainty about certification," said one Bogota broker.
U.S. President Bill Clinton is due to announce which countries he will certify Friday. Renewed decertification for Colombia could trigger economic sanctions, U.S. officials have threatened.
The day's main gainer was cement manufacturer Cemento Argos, which posted a 9 percent rise in net profits in 1996 compared to 1995.
It was up 2.23 percent to 7,780 on the Bogota exchange and up 1.57 percent on the Medellin exchange to 7,750.
Banco de Bogota dipped 0.77 percent to 6,300 in Bogota and dropped 1.41 percent to 6,310 in Medellin.
Supermarket chain Carulla fell 1.65 percent to 4,150 in Bogota and slipped back 0.04 percent in Medellin to 6,772.
